topic: A person discovers the tree they planted as a child has been cut down
text: Well, ain't that the way. I remember when you planted that tree, barely taller than a spindly arm, just a slip of a thing. You must've been no more than knee-high to a chicken, and here I was, showing you how to settle the roots in the soil, pat it down, give it a good drink. You were so eager, grinning from ear to ear, talking about how one day it'd be big enough to shade the whole field. I told you, "This tree, it's a mark of your hands, your sweat, a piece of you in the earth." Even if the tree's gone, the spot where it stood, it's still a part of you, a story to tell. You grew alongside that tree, and now, even without it, you're tall and strong, just like it would've been.
